text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.08% today to $135.72, giving back some of yesterday's gains despite oil prices holding relatively steady. The stock had surged 0.8% yesterday as geopolitical tensions between Iran and Kuwait pushed U.S. crude up sharply, but today's pullback came as oil markets stabilized—the U.S. benchmark at $91.48 is essentially flat from yesterday, and Trump's public assurance that renewed Mideast hostilities won't last "too long" appears to have eased some of the crisis premium that had built into prices.

The broader context is that oil majors like ConocoPhillips benefited from the week's 9% gain in crude prices, but energy stocks are now vulnerable to any signal—whether political statements or simply a lack of fresh escalation—that the geopolitical premium could deflate. Today's move reflects profit-taking after a sharp run-up rather than any fundamental shift in the company's operations.
